decisions.reason: Preserving the complete letterform geometry during the kerning study does not change the accent's existing literal-derivation rules.
The task-local instruction to preserve current geometry during spacing variations leaves the Hero V's persistent master geometry unchanged.
The kerning-study constraint preserves rather than modifies the current optically drawn second-V construction.
Holding the E and L geometry fixed for the kerning studies does not alter their persistent architectural construction requirements.
The exact-geometry constraint preserves the established height hierarchy without changing any hierarchy attribute.
The source preserves the existing geometry and therefore leaves the established Hero-V-to-accent peak alignment unchanged.
The existing message-187 MODIFY already records side-by-side kerning variations and the identical-geometry comparison constraint.
The existing message-187 MODIFY already captures the new spacing direction; preserving geometry adds no further kerning-state change.
The geometry-preservation policy does not change the selected champagne-gold distribution, which is separately recorded from the same message.
The geometry-preservation policy does not change the selected Satin Reflection finish, which is separately recorded from the same message.
The kerning-study geometry constraint has no effect on accepted review-image delivery formats.
Varying only spacing preserves the existing shared-baseline requirement and introduces no baseline update.
